releases.body:
Feature release: adds the `Muse Agent` row to `/connect` and fixes the allowance warning so it no longer repeats a window that has already reset. Version 1.1.0 is already on npm; this GitHub Release documents what shipped from commit `0f04fbd` (tag `v1.1.0`).

### What changed

- `/connect` gains a `Muse Agent` row, shaped like opencode's `claude-agent` integration: one external method, "Muse CLI login (`muse login`)". Connecting records the choice only. The credential stays with `muse login`, and the stored connection is `{"type": "external", "methodID": "muse-login"}` with no secret. The provider names that row with `integrationID: "muse-agent"`, so the picker and `/connect` share one identity; the provider id remains `muse` and stays `activation: "enabled"`, so the link cannot hide models when no connection exists.
- The row reports a missing login. A read-only probe (`muse usage --json`, no model turn) distinguishes "not logged in" from everything else; only that answer sets `needs_auth`, rendered as "Sign in required →". Offline, timeout, or a renamed subcommand leaves the row untouched, and a successful login clears it. A finished turn updates the same status without running the CLI, so a login that expired mid-session is noticed.
- `checkAllowance` skips a window that has already reset instead of repeating a stale percentage and reset time. `usage/read` answers from the host's observation, so an idle host could carry a 95% window whose reset was days past; the line now also names the observation's age, e.g. `(observed 3h 05m ago)`.

### Verification

Measured on opencode 2.4.1 on 2026-11-25: the row reaches `GET /api/integration` after plugin activation; `opencode auth login muse-agent --method muse-login` connects; one `muse/muse-ember-1.0` turn still completes. The user's `~/.config/muse/auth.json` and `settings.json` hashes were unchanged.

### Published artifact

- `dist/` hashes to `3175a42…` (168 files), built from the committed lockfile with node v24.22.1, npm 11.19.1, and tsc 5.9.3
- npm shasum `b4badf06c5248148cd30b1a0ba36a8603013562d`
- integrity `sha512-2zC6xXHM+bSllQs1mW842CVFzrfreebuHMeUcJVsB+QAm4o//+jj+6I1KRUhCxktBM//bF/yCiFQwHFHnO92kQ==`
- Source: commit `0f04fbd9245da10bc42a40c572429bd2bb7c6b16`, tag `v1.1.0`
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@jonathand34/opencode-plugin-muse/v/1.1.0

### Compatibility

Package name, `.` and `./tui` exports, and provider id `muse` are unchanged from `1.0.0`. Since `1.0.1`: the feature work is PR #18 (`release/1.1.0`) and the allowance fix is PR #19 (`fix/allowance-stale-window`); #13-#17 are docs-only (published 1.0.1 record, npm rendering verification, owner-run turn, and README rationale).

releases.name: v1.0.1 — docs-only: the README npm should have shown
releases.body:
Documentation-only patch. The plugin code is unchanged: `dist/` hashes to
`3fef9808acc1c6b0b1fcbf49b9eaa49fafc58d0c2443395a6389a73b0a350669` across its
160 files, the same value recorded for `1.0.0`, so no live turn was re-run for
this release and the `1.0.0` compatibility promise is untouched.

What changed is what the npm page shows. npm renders the `README.md` inside the
published tarball and cannot be edited in place, so the `1.0.0` page still
carried a README written before the demo, the quickstart, and the
`opencode.jsonc` pin existed. `1.0.1` publishes the current README with the demo
GIF inline and adds `homepage`, so the package page links both the repository and
the README.

### Published artifact

- Tarball sha256 `e32f0ee0468519ab7d87230c072725d62ab2f1192a7468b4669c2e5bde5f9765`,
  201,075 bytes, 165 files
- npm shasum `6c27c8d0bd6461053fa6e0b149bc444bc798102c`
- Staged by CI run [45460239694](https://github.com/jond34/opencode-plugin-muse/actions/runs/45460239694)
  on `b15ba82`, downloaded and matched to a clean local rebuild byte for byte,
  then approved with 2FA
- The SLSA v1 provenance attestation names `b15ba82`, and `npm audit signatures`
  verifies it

### Not in this release

No source, `dist/`, dependency, export, provider id, or documented `MUSE_*`
variable changed. `docs/comparison.md` and `docs/provenance.md` keep their
`1.0.0` records, because those record what was verified then.

First stable release of the cleaned public tree. The package name, `.` and
`./tui` exports, provider id `muse`, documented `MUSE_*` variables, and the
install command are the compatibility promise; model ids and vendor behavior
remain data.

X9a passed on 2026-11-24 with opencode 2.4.1 and Muse CLI 1.4.25: a simple turn,
a bridged `shell` call, and a resumed turn all returned the expected nonce. X9b
then installed the published `1.0.0` and returned an exact nonce in a run that
loaded only that package. The package compiles against `@opencode/plugin` 2.3.2
and `@muse-code/sdk` 1.4.24; that pair was not live-run in this pass. On 2.4.1,
`opencode models` does not list the plugin-injected `muse/*` provider, but a
direct `opencode run -m muse/...` resolves it.

### Containment and private host configuration

- The plugin starts `muse serve` with a private config directory, so Muse's own
  skills, observer reminders, workflow triggers, context slimming, and foreign
  personal skills are off and opencode owns the context around the model.
- The bridge's toolset is pinned to `mcp__opencode__*`. Muse's own spawner tools
  stay outside it; every bridged call is emitted into opencode and crosses
  opencode's permission engine.
- Project-supplied Muse hooks are refused unless their exact hash is trusted
  with `bun run doctor --trust-hooks` or `MUSE_ALLOW_PROJECT_HOOKS=1` is set for
  one run. Installed plugin handlers remain allowed and are reported by origin.

### Known limitation

- A Muse plugin hook approved in your Muse config does not run in opencode
  sessions: the plugin starts the host with a private config, so the host sees
  no approval. A private config that holds its own approval is amnestied by
  `muse plugins update` on 1.4.25; this plugin never creates or updates one.
  `bun run doctor` reports an installed plugin handler with this limitation.

### opencode-owned context and native history

- Titles and compaction are answered inside opencode. Titles are derived from
  the first user message; compaction is a deterministic transcript digest, so
  neither spends a Muse turn.
- The visible transcript is fingerprinted. A rewritten or compacted history
  retires the native session and reseeds from the full prompt instead of
  silently continuing a different conversation.
- Native history remains opt-in. The digest is the fallback when it is off.

### Effort, prompt, and history boundaries

- A request's `model.variant` is resolved to Muse's closed effort vocabulary and
  sent as `reasoningEffort`; `default` omits the field, and an unavailable tier
  fails closed instead of falling to the lowest tier.
- Agent and instruction text travel as `SessionConfig.developerPrompt` on start
  and resume, so the first user turn is not prefixed.
- A primary request with no bridge tools fails before `session/start` with an
  actionable error. A rewritten history reseeds; the measured fork path was
  removed because it cost more input than a reseed.
- Images remain the only attachment kind. There is no PDF or text-file surface.

### Limits that did not change

- No Windows desktop parity. The runner matrix and installer checks do not
  become a desktop claim.
- No containment behind the bridge. opencode's permission rules are the gate,
  and `allowAll` remains the Muse-side mode.
- No per-turn cost cap, no offline path, and no native-history default change.

### Install

```bash
opencode plugin add @jonathand34/opencode-plugin-muse@1.0.0
```

### Provenance

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@jonathand34/opencode-plugin-muse/v/1.0.0
- Source: commit `af503fdc4462f035caa1a68300764522cdae2c83`, tag `v1.0.0`
- Provenance: https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/@jonathand34%2fopencode-plugin-muse@1.0.0
- X9 evidence: `docs/evidence/2026-11-24-r36-x9.json`
